rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's mercy and providence entail a day that rewards the grateful and punishes the ungrateful; treating them alike would contradict divine justice.
rows.anchor: Another natural consequence of God’s mercy and providence is that He bring about A Day in which He reward

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The harmony of night and day and apparently opposed cosmic elements shows that a wise, exalted sovereign orders them together as creator and master of all.
rows.anchor: The harmony between the night and the day which is a means to nurture and nourish man shows that various elements of this universe

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier peoples rejected God's signs and strayed; Quraysh will face their fate if they follow the same course after rejecting the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: A warning is sound to the Quraysh in this verse: the way they have lost their senses

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse renews monotheism and the Hereafter: earth and sky form a coherent dwelling under one God's rule, since rival gods could not produce their harmony.
rows.anchor: It is God Who has made this house and it is He alone Whose rule prevails

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created humans in a form better than all other creations.
rows.anchor: after bringing into existence a decorated and embellished house God created man and created him in a form better than

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iḥsān means doing something in a befitting manner; 95:4 is cited as a parallel statement that humans were created in the finest mould.
rows.anchor: means “to do something in a befitting manner.” At another instance, this topic is discussed in the following words

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The finest mould concerns more than appearance: the fitting proportion of bodily material and human abilities makes people superior to other worldly creations.
rows.anchor: of moulds here obviously does not refer merely to man’s appearance; it also refers

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As God prepared a beautifully adorned dwelling, He also provided people with pure sustenance.
rows.anchor: He also provided them with sustenance of pure things.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording identifies God as Lord of people and the universe, and as blessed and munificent.
rows.anchor: God is the Lord of people as well as of the universe and He is very blessed and munificent.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone truly lives and gives life; the other beings worshipped are lifeless, cannot hear or help, and should not be invoked. Worship, obedience, and gratitude belong to God alone.
rows.anchor: They neither hear nor are able to help anyone. It is fruitless whether they are called or not.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to declare that he will not worship the opponents' deities despite pressure: clear signs have come, and he is commanded to submit only to God.
rows.anchor: I have been forbidden to worship which you invoke besides God now that clear signs have come to me from my Lord.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Parts of the verse are ellipted according to conventional Arabic style; the author says he supplies such expressions here and has given parallels elsewhere in the commentary.
rows.anchor: I have tried to reveal these expressions and at other instances of this exegesis

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reflecting on the phases of human creation suffices to point to God's power and wisdom and to belief in monotheism and the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: they are sufficient to point to God’s power and wisdom as well as to belief in monotheism and hereafter.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first human was created from clay; later generations begin as a drop of fluid, become a clot and fetus, and emerge from the womb as living infants.
rows.anchor: the Almighty began man’s creation with clay; the later generations were born through a drop of fluid.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before the clauses about reaching adolescence and becoming old, the text suppresses the subject: God nourishes people and grants them time.
rows.anchor: the subject of nourishing them and giving them time is suppressed before

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not every infant reaches adolescence, and no one receives an unlimited lifespan; a clause saying many are given time is suppressed before the phrase about reaching adolescence.
rows.anchor: it is not always the case that each infant reaches adolescence.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “so that you may understand” has omitted wording that explains the purpose of life's stages: people are to reflect on their creation and recognize their Lord's power and wisdom.
rows.anchor: allude to the reason because of which the Almighty has made man pass through these ups and downs of life.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God formed the world as the best means for people to learn the truths necessary for their well-being and salvation.
rows.anchor: it has become the best source of learning all the facts which are necessary for the well-being and salvation of man.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who controls life, death, youth, old age, and each lifespan has no partner and will certainly resurrect and gather people for account; this is no difficulty for Him.
rows.anchor: He shall one day necessarily gather people to take account from them and this task is not the least difficult for Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Life and death are wholly under God's control; nothing blocks His will, and He will bring the Hereafter into being instantly by command.
rows.anchor: He need only say: “Be,” and it is done and is done in a manner He wants.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the signs are clear, the disputants have lost their senses and indulge in frivolous talk to deny them.
rows.anchor: these wretched people have lost their senses because they are indulging in frivolous talk

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The Book” refers to the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: refers to the Qur’ ān. These verses state their crime: they not only rejected the Qur’ ān, they also rejected all the teachings

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers reject both the Qur'an and the teachings delivered by all messengers; since the prophets taught the same basic message, rejecting the Qur'an amounts to rejecting them all.
rows.anchor: so rejecting the Qur’ ān is like rejecting all the prophets.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word “soon” is a threat that the deniers will soon see the consequence of rejecting the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: are a threat. If they dare reject the Qur’ ān, they will soon see the fate of this rejection.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi says “their feet” is suppressed after “chains” and translates the verse with that ellipsis supplied.
rows.anchor: their necks shall be shackled and their feet shall be enchained.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because they arrogantly denied God's signs, necks will be shackled, feet chained, and they will be dragged through boiling water before being cast into Hell.
rows.anchor: their necks shall be shackled and their feet shall be enchained. After that, they will be dragged into boiling water

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression “sajara al-tannūr” means that a kiln was filled with fuel.
rows.anchor: means “the kiln was filled with fuel.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those besides God” refers here to people or beings who oppose God.
rows.anchor: here refers to those who oppose God and it is used in this meaning.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolaters first admit they worshipped deities that cannot help them, then deny having worshipped anything when they realize that this worship led to their punishment; Qur'anic scenes show them affirming and disavowing their deities in the same breath.
rows.anchor: at first they will acknowledge that they had some deities whom they worshipped but that none of them is here to help them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Thus” points to the simultaneous acknowledgment and denial; punishment so confuses the idolaters that they lose track of what they have said, a theme revisited at 41:40.
rows.anchor: allude to this very simultaneous acknowledgement and denial: the punishment of the Almighty will make them so badly lose their wits

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their fate follows from baseless pride: blessings belonged to God and called for gratitude and obedience, but they treated them as entitlements and arrogantly insulted the messengers who reminded them.
rows.anchor: the result of their baseless arrogance and conceit. Whatever they had been blessed with in the previous world was never owned by them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God alone owns the heavens and earth, pride belongs to Him alone; another's claim to this exclusive divine quality is baseless and amounts to polytheism.
rows.anchor: Hence conceit is only befitting for Him and no one else.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He alludes to a report describing divine greatness as God's exclusive robe to explain why pride belongs to God alone.
rows.anchor: the words of the following narrative allude to

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At this point excuses are useless: the arrogant are told to enter Hell's gates and remain there forever, an evil abode.
rows.anchor: The implication is that presenting any excuse at this time is of no use.
